title: Linear Algebra I
source_note: Standard NUC-aligned Nigerian university 200L Linear Algebra I curriculum: vector spaces and subspaces, linear independence/span/basis/dimension, matrix algebra, determinants, and solving systems of linear equations by Gaussian elimination.

questions.question: Which of the following is required for a set V with operations + and scalar multiplication to be a vector space over a field F?
options: V must be closed under vector addition and scalar multiplication, and satisfy the vector space axioms (associativity, identity, inverses, distributivity, etc.)
V must contain only finite sets of numbers
V must have exactly one element
Scalar multiplication must always give zero
questions.correct_answer: V must be closed under vector addition and scalar multiplication, and satisfy the vector space axioms (associativity, identity, inverses, distributivity, etc.)
questions.explanation: A vector space is defined by closure under the two operations together with the standard list of axioms including additive identity/inverse and distributive laws.

questions.question: A non-empty subset W of a vector space V is a subspace of V if and only if:
options: W is closed under vector addition and scalar multiplication
W contains only the zero vector
W has more elements than V
W is closed under matrix multiplication only
questions.correct_answer: W is closed under vector addition and scalar multiplication
questions.explanation: The subspace test requires closure under the two vector space operations (which also forces 0 ∈ W); the other vector space axioms are automatically inherited from V.

questions.question: Which of the following subsets of ℝ^3 is a subspace of ℝ^3?
questions.explanation: This is a homogeneous linear equation through the origin, which is closed under addition and scalar multiplication; the others fail because they don't contain the zero vector or aren't closed.

questions.question: A set of vectors {v1, v2, ..., vn} is linearly independent if:
options: The only solution to c1v1 + c2v2 + ... + cnvn = 0 is c1 = c2 = ... = cn = 0
At least one vector is a scalar multiple of another
Some ci can be nonzero and the sum still equals 0
questions.correct_answer: The only solution to c1v1 + c2v2 + ... + cnvn = 0 is c1 = c2 = ... = cn = 0
questions.explanation: Linear independence means no nontrivial linear combination of the vectors gives the zero vector.

questions.question: In ℝ^3, are the vectors (1, 0, 0), (0, 1, 0), and (1, 1, 0) linearly independent?
options: No, because they are all unit vectors
questions.explanation: Since the third vector is a linear combination of the first two, there is a nontrivial dependence relation, so the set is linearly dependent.

questions.question: A basis of a vector space V is:
options: A linearly independent set that spans V
Any set that spans V, whether independent or not
A set containing only the zero vector
The largest possible subset of V
questions.correct_answer: A linearly independent set that spans V
questions.explanation: A basis must be both linearly independent and a spanning set, so every vector in V is a unique linear combination of basis vectors.

questions.question: What is the dimension of ℝ^4 as a vector space over ℝ?
questions.explanation: The standard basis {e1, e2, e3, e4} has 4 vectors, so dim(ℝ^4) = 4.

questions.question: If a vector space V has dimension n, then any linearly independent set of exactly n vectors in V:
options: Is automatically a basis of V
questions.correct_answer: Is automatically a basis of V
questions.explanation: In an n-dimensional space, any linearly independent set of n vectors automatically spans the space and is therefore a basis.

questions.question: For two matrices A and B to be multiplied as AB, what condition must hold on their dimensions?
options: The number of columns of A must equal the number of rows of B
A and B must have the same dimensions
The number of rows of A must equal the number of rows of B
A and B must both be square
questions.correct_answer: The number of columns of A must equal the number of rows of B
questions.explanation: Matrix multiplication AB is only defined when A is m×n and B is n×p, i.e. the inner dimensions match.

questions.question: If A is a 2×3 matrix and B is a 3×4 matrix, what are the dimensions of AB?
questions.explanation: The product of an m×n matrix and an n×p matrix is an m×p matrix, so 2×3 times 3×4 gives 2×4.

questions.question: In general, for matrices A and B (where both products are defined), which is true?
options: AB ≠ BA in general (matrix multiplication is not commutative)
AB and BA always have the same dimensions
Matrix multiplication is always commutative for square matrices
questions.correct_answer: AB ≠ BA in general (matrix multiplication is not commutative)
questions.explanation: Unlike scalar multiplication, matrix multiplication does not commute in general, even for square matrices.

questions.question: What is the determinant of the matrix [[3, 1], [2, 4]]?
A square matrix A has an inverse A⁻¹ if and only if:
questions.correct_answer: det(A) ≠ 0
questions.explanation: A square matrix is invertible (non-singular) precisely when its determinant is nonzero.

questions.question: What is the inverse of the 2×2 identity matrix I?
questions.correct_answer: I itself
questions.explanation: The identity matrix is its own inverse since I × I = I.

questions.question: For a 3×3 matrix A, if two rows are identical, what is det(A)?
options: It equals the trace of A
questions.explanation: A determinant is zero whenever two rows (or columns) of the matrix are identical, since the rows become linearly dependent.

questions.question: Which elementary row operation does NOT change the determinant of a matrix?
options: Adding a multiple of one row to another row
Multiplying a row by a nonzero scalar k
questions.correct_answer: Adding a multiple of one row to another row
questions.explanation: Adding a scalar multiple of one row to another leaves the determinant unchanged; swapping rows negates it, and scaling a row by k multiplies the determinant by k.

questions.question: Using Gaussian elimination, a system of linear equations is transformed into:
options: Row echelon form, from which solutions can be found by back-substitution
A single equation with no solution
questions.correct_answer: Row echelon form, from which solutions can be found by back-substitution
questions.explanation: Gaussian elimination applies elementary row operations to reduce the augmented matrix to row echelon form, after which back-substitution solves the system.

questions.question: Solve the system x + y = 5, x − y = 1 for x and y.
questions.explanation: Adding the equations gives 2x = 6, so x = 3; substituting gives y = 5 − 3 = 2.

questions.question: A system of linear equations Ax = b is called consistent if:
options: It has at least one solution
questions.correct_answer: It has at least one solution
questions.explanation: Consistency simply means a solution (unique or infinitely many) exists; an inconsistent system has no solution.

questions.question: If a homogeneous system Ax = 0 has only the trivial solution x = 0, what does this imply about the columns of A?
options: The columns of A are linearly independent
The columns of A are linearly dependent
A must be a non-square matrix
questions.correct_answer: The columns of A are linearly independent
questions.explanation: The only solution being trivial means no nontrivial linear combination of the columns gives zero, i.e. the columns are linearly independent.

questions.question: The rank of a matrix A is defined as:
options: The maximum number of linearly independent rows (or equivalently columns) of A
The number of rows of A
The sum of the diagonal entries of A
questions.correct_answer: The maximum number of linearly independent rows (or equivalently columns) of A
questions.explanation: The rank equals the dimension of the row space (which equals the dimension of the column space), i.e. the number of linearly independent rows/columns.

questions.question: What is the rank of the 3×3 identity matrix I3?
questions.explanation: All three rows of the identity matrix are linearly independent, so its rank equals its size, 3.

questions.question: By the Rank-Nullity Theorem, for an m×n matrix A, rank(A) + nullity(A) equals:
options: n (the number of columns of A)
m (the number of rows of A)
questions.correct_answer: n (the number of columns of A)
questions.explanation: The rank-nullity theorem states that rank(A) + nullity(A) = n, where n is the number of columns (the dimension of the domain).

questions.question: The transpose of a matrix A, denoted A^T, is obtained by:
options: Interchanging the rows and columns of A
Multiplying every entry of A by −1
Reversing the order of the rows only
questions.correct_answer: Interchanging the rows and columns of A
questions.explanation: The transpose swaps rows for columns, so the (i,j) entry of A becomes the (j,i) entry of A^T.

questions.question: A square matrix A is called symmetric if:
questions.correct_answer: A = A^T
questions.explanation: Symmetric matrices are equal to their own transpose, meaning a_ij = a_ji for all i, j.

questions.question: What is the trace of the matrix [[2, 5], [7, 3]]?
questions.explanation: The trace is the sum of the diagonal entries: 2 + 3 = 5.

questions.question: Cramer's rule for solving a system of n linear equations in n unknowns can be applied when:
options: The coefficient matrix has a nonzero determinant
The system has infinitely many solutions
questions.correct_answer: The coefficient matrix has a nonzero determinant
questions.explanation: Cramer's rule requires det(A) ≠ 0 so that x_i = det(A_i)/det(A) is well-defined for a unique solution.

questions.question: For an m×n matrix representing a linear map from ℝ^n to ℝ^m, the set of all solutions x to Ax = 0 is called:
questions.correct_answer: The null space (kernel) of A
questions.explanation: The null space (or kernel) consists precisely of all vectors x mapped to the zero vector by A.

questions.question: What is the span of the vectors (1, 0) and (0, 1) in ℝ^2?
questions.correct_answer: All of ℝ^2
questions.explanation: Since (1,0) and (0,1) form the standard basis of ℝ^2, every vector in ℝ^2 can be written as a linear combination of them.

questions.question: If A and B are both n×n invertible matrices, then (AB)⁻¹ equals:
questions.correct_answer: B⁻¹A⁻¹
questions.explanation: The inverse of a product reverses the order: (AB)(B⁻¹A⁻¹) = A(BB⁻¹)A⁻¹ = AA⁻¹ = I.

questions.question: Using the adjugate (adjoint) method, the inverse of a square matrix A is given by:
options: A⁻¹ = adj(A) alone, regardless of det(A)
questions.correct_answer: A⁻¹ = (1/det(A)) × adj(A)
questions.explanation: The classical adjoint formula expresses the inverse as the adjugate matrix scaled by the reciprocal of the determinant.

questions.question: How many solutions does the system x + y = 2, 2x + 2y = 4 have?
questions.correct_answer: Infinitely many
questions.explanation: The second equation is just twice the first, so both equations describe the same line; every point on that line is a solution.
